key_insight: GazeRIB trains chest X-ray models by masking regions radiologists did not view, then uses full images at inference. The study systematically tests how the choice and number of readers affect gaze-guided learning, though the provided abstract is truncated before reporting results.
problem_solved: The value of radiologist gaze as training supervision may depend on whose attention is captured and how many readers contribute—factors that have not been systematically tested.
method: Collect repeated gaze readings from eight experts examining the same 80 chest X-rays.
Apply Gaze-guided Radiologist-Informed Blackout to mask unviewed regions during training while leaving inference images unmasked.
Compare individual readers with three-, five-, and eight-reader panels across seven architectures and 10 seeds, evaluating 910 models.
impact: This evaluation can help practitioners assess reader-panel design when incorporating expert attention into medical image learning. Its training-only masking approach requires no gaze input at inference.
visual_elements: Side-by-side chest X-rays showing a gaze overlay, training blackout mask, and unmasked inference image.
Reader-panel icons comparing one, three, five, and eight experts.
Experiment grid highlighting seven architectures, 10 seeds, and 910 evaluated models.
Workflow diagram: expert gaze collection → training masks → model training → full-image inference.
paper_title: GazeRIB: Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Reader Gaze-Guided Chest X-ray Learning
paper_authors: Nattakorn Kittisut, Roy M. Gabriel, Marly van Assen, Mohammadreza Zandehshahvar, Carlo N. De Cecco
